key_insight: A camera-specific reward-feedback loop improves camera controllability in video diffusion models by evaluating and optimizing camera alignment efficiently, without repeatedly decoding latents to RGB.
problem_solved: Existing reward-feedback (ReFL) methods can’t effectively or efficiently evaluate video-camera alignment because general reward models lack camera-awareness and decoding latents into RGB for reward computation is computationally expensive.
method: Train or adapt a lightweight, camera-aware reward model that directly assesses video-camera alignment (poses, motion, framing) rather than generic video quality.
Compute rewards in latent space or with efficient proxies to avoid repeated expensive RGB decoding, enabling frequent feedback during fine-tuning.
Integrate the camera reward into a ReFL-style training loop to fine-tune the diffusion model for stronger and more consistent camera control.
impact: Enables practitioners to achieve more reliable and controllable camera behavior in generated videos with far less compute overhead, improving applicability of video diffusion models for filmmaking, robotics simulation, and interactive content creation.
visual_elements: Before/After frame sequence: side-by-side short clips showing improved camera framing and motion alignment.
Training loop diagram: diffusion model → latent-space reward evaluator → reward feedback → fine-tuning (highlighting no RGB decode step).
Architecture sketch: camera-aware reward model inputs (latent video + camera params) and outputs a scalar alignment score.
Bar chart or radar plot: comparison of camera-alignment metrics and compute cost (decoding vs latent reward) across methods.
paper_title: CamPilot: Improving Camera Control in Video Diffusion Model with Efficient Camera Reward Feedback
paper_authors: Wenhang Ge, Guibao Shen, Jiawei Feng, Luozhou Wang, Hao Lu
